findings.claim: The new substitution scan runs only inside segments that msysSegments keeps. msysSegments drops a segment that is all assignments and includes MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=… (line 905), and a segment whose own prefix opts out (segmentOptsOut, line 918). In both cases the $( … ) bodies inside that segment are never scanned. But the shell does not apply that opt-out to a gh that runs inside the substitution: a prefix assignment reaches only the outer command, and an assignment-only statement exports nothing. The result: misapplying the row's own cure (MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1) to the exact 2026-10-16 trigger shape is allowed, and the post is munged. This breaks the invariant's clause 'unless MSYS_NO_PATHCONV is set where the shell would apply it'.
findings.counterexample: Probe cases2: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 u1=$(gh pr comment 1560 -R o/r --body '/gemini review') && echo ok returns allow/no-match. cases1: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 u=$(gh … --body /y), MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 echo $(gh … --body /y), env MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 echo $(gh …) and MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 gh pr comment 5 --body "$(gh pr comment 6 --body /y)" all return allow/no-match. Measured with argv-echo: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 u1=$(node argv-echo.mjs '/gemini review') gives C:/Program Files/Git/gemini review; the prefix-on-echo form, the env-prefix form and the prefix-on-outer-node form each give X:/; u=$(MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 node … '/gemini review') gives /gemini review (so the committed negative control is right). No test pins the misplaced opt-out. Shape of a fix: scan the substitution bodies of every tokenized segment, applying only the opt-out state that the body itself or an earlier export establishes, rather than only the segments msysSegments keeps.

findings.claim: The locator treats literal text as a substitution. It looks for $( and backticks in blankSingleQuoted(seg.raw). That text keeps an escaped \$( and an escaped backtick (blankSingleQuoted copies the backslash and the next character as a pair; indexOf still finds the $( or the backtick). It also keeps comment text, because tokenizeShell drops comment tokens but seg.raw still contains the comment. So a gh command quoted as inline markdown code in a double-quoted body, or named in a comment, is denied. The shell never runs that gh, and MSYS leaves the outer body correct. This is a regression the fold introduced: bdab5216 allowed these shapes. It breaks the invariant's 'that the shell would not run as a gh invocation, is allowed', in the shape a disposition comment about this incident would take.
findings.counterexample: Probe cases2: gh pr comment 5 --body "Posted via \`gh pr comment 5 --body '/gemini review'\` which munged" returns deny, matched --body /gemini review\`, where old returns allow. gh pr comment 5 --body "The \$(gh api x -f body=/y) form" returns deny, where old returns allow. gh api …/comments -f "body=The \`gh api -f body=/x\` form" returns deny via the inner scan; the outer head body=The is not munged. cases1: echo hi # $(gh pr comment 5 --body /x) returns deny; a newline then # run \`gh pr comment 5 --body /gemini review\` later returns deny; echo "\$(gh …)" returns deny. Measured: echo "literal: \`node argv-echo.mjs /x\` and \$(node argv-echo.mjs /y)" printed both literally, so nothing ran. The rule is fail-closed and the --body-file cure works, so this is an over-deny, not an over-allow.

findings.claim: The scan runs on text with the heredoc bodies blanked out. Bash expands $( … ) inside an unquoted heredoc and runs it, so a gh inside one is allowed. The comment does not disclose this; it discloses only a variable or substitution VALUE.
findings.counterexample: Probe cases1: cat <<EOF, a line $(gh pr comment 5 --body /x), EOF returns allow/no-match. Measured: the same heredoc with $(node argv-echo.mjs /x) printed X:/. The quoted <<'EOF' form is correctly allowed.

findings.claim: programIndex still misses several shapes in which the shell runs gh. (a) The .exe check is case-sensitive, so GH.EXE and gh.EXE are missed. (b) A quoted Windows path with backslashes is missed. (c) gh after case … in pat), after f() {, after time -p, and inside a process substitution <( … ) (the locator only looks for $() is missed. Separately, X=1 if gh … is denied, although bash runs if as an ordinary command there (not found, rc 127) and gh never runs. That is a negligible over-deny.
findings.counterexample: Probe cases1, all allow/no-match: GH.EXE pr comment 5 --body /x, gh.EXE …, 'C:\Program Files\GitHub CLI\gh.exe' pr comment 5 --body /x, case a in a) gh … --body /x ;; esac, f() { gh … --body /x; }; f, time -p gh … --body /x, cat <(gh … --body /x). Measured, each run and converted: NODE.EXE and Node.Exe argv-echo /x gave X:/; the Windows-path C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe gave X:/; the case, function, process-substitution and time -p forms gave Z:/, W:/, V:/, U:/. X=1 if node … gave 'if: command not found'. $'it\'s' $(gh …) (blankSingleQuoted does not know ANSI-C quoting) also allows; measured: the gh-like call ran (Y:/).

findings.claim: Pre-existing, not introduced by the fold, but inside the invariant as stated ('--body/-b begins with /'): the glued short form -b/x is not read by optionsAsWritten, and MSYS converts it.
findings.counterexample: Probe cases1: gh pr comment 5 -b/x returns allow/no-match. Measured: argv-echo -b/x gave -bX:/.

findings.claim: Two documentation gaps. (a) The new RESERVED_BEFORE_PROGRAM const was inserted between programIndex's JSDoc and the function, so that JSDoc now attaches to the const. It also still says 'after any VAR=VALUE assignments and known wrappers', with no mention of reserved words or .exe. (b) The changeset describes only the msys-body-slash row. Because programIndex is shared, sed-i-escape and inline-body-escape now deny shapes they used to allow; the changeset does not mention that.
findings.counterexample: sed -n 660,672p shows the docstring followed directly by the const's own JSDoc. Probe cases1: { sed -i 's/\(a\)/x/' f; } returns deny/sed-i-escape; then node -e 'a\d' and time node.exe -e 'a\d' return deny/inline-body-escape; old returns allow for all three. The new denies are correct; only the changeset text omits them.

verdict: read 2 on 1e36ff59 (scoped to the fold bdab5216..1e36ff59): as typed, 0 BLOCKING, 2 MATERIAL, 4 MINOR, 0 QUESTION; the leg named the rule not converged at MATERIAL and recommended one more read scoped to the F1/F2 fold. Held at source (the leg's probe evaluated each command through the built dist and through the two commits' sources transpiled into scratch, and re-measured every shell claim with the argv-echo script): the exact 2026-10-16 trigger chain denies with matched --body /gemini review; backtick, double-quoted $( ), arithmetic-wrapped, multiple-backtick, quoted-paren and unterminated forms deny; a body split by ; | && inside the substitution denies; nesting two and four deep denies and five allows per the disclosed cap; every reserved word before gh denies and a reserved word as an argument allows; gh.exe and a /c/… path to it deny; the field predicate holds on =/x, tab and newline after the first whitespace, the typed and raw @ forms, workflow run and workflow view; the opt-out inside the substitution and an export before it allow; single quotes and bash -c stay literal; the other rows gained no false positives and their new denies are shapes the shell runs; the red check's three failing blocks are the right three; the comment's measurements and the changeset's predicate text match the code. Folded by the seat in the next commit: F1 MATERIAL (a segment the opt-out prefix covers or that is all assignments with the opt-out had its substitution bodies skipped although the shell runs them first, without the prefix — msysSegments now returns such segments flagged when asked and the row descends into their substitutions while skipping their token scan), F2 MATERIAL (an escaped \$( or backtick in a double-quoted body and a $( inside a comment were read as substitutions — an opener behind an odd run of backslashes is skipped and comments are blanked before locating), F4 in part (GH.EXE and a quoted Windows path with backslashes, a function header, time -p), F5 (the glued -b/x short body), F6 (the programIndex JSDoc restored to the function and naming the shared effect; the changeset names the sed-i-escape and inline-body-escape rows' new reads). Declined with the reason: F3 (a $( … ) inside an unquoted heredoc body is hidden by the heredoc blanking; disclosed in the row's comment, not read), F4's process substitution, case patterns and ANSI-C quoting (rare; disclosed).
